meta.title: Road signs
meta.summary: You will learn to recognise the 7 groups of signs, understand where the zone of application of prohibitory signs ends, who they do not apply to, what plates change and which signal takes precedence when they conflict.

p: In the Rules, road signs are divided into 7 groups, and a sign number always starts with the number of its group: 1 - warning signs, 2 - priority signs, 3 - prohibitory signs, 4 - mandatory signs, 5 - information signs, 6 - service signs, 7 - additional information plates.

Shape and colour tell you the meaning before you make out the picture. A white triangle with a red border means “danger ahead”. A white circle with a red border means “not allowed”. A blue circle means “only this way”. A blue rectangle means information or a special traffic regime. A blue rectangle with a white field means a service. A white plate under a sign clarifies it. At road works and where traffic is temporarily changed, temporary signs on a yellow background are used ⟦12⟧.

The numbers of some signs in Kazakhstan differ from the Russian ones. For example, the “Speed hump” sign is 1.16.1 here, the “Pedestrian crossing” sign is 5.16.1 and 5.16.2, and the “Residential zone” sign is 5.38. In the test, follow the Kazakhstan numbering.
lesson.tip: Look at the shape and colour first, then at the picture: that way you can tell a sign's group in a second.

p: They warn you in advance about a hazardous section so that you have time to slow down and prepare. On their own they prohibit nothing, but the general rules still apply: for example, at a dangerous bend with visibility of less than 100 m you must not stop, and you must not overtake by moving into the oncoming lane ⟦13⟧.

Outside built-up areas, signs 1.1, 1.2 and 1.5-1.30 are placed 150-300 m before the hazardous place; in a built-up area and a residential zone, 50-100 m before it. If the distance is different, it is shown on plate 7.1.1. Plate 7.2.1 with arrows shows the length of the hazardous section.

Signs 1.13 “Steep descent” and 1.14 “Steep ascent” may stand right at the start of the slope if descents and ascents follow one another. Sign 1.23 for short-term works may stand only 10-15 m before the works. Outside built-up areas, signs 1.1, 1.2, 1.9, 1.10, 1.21 and 1.23 are repeated: the second sign is placed at least 50 m before the hazardous section.
list: 1.1 and 1.2 - a level crossing with and without a barrier. Outside built-up areas they are supplemented by signs 1.4.1-1.4.6 with red stripes: three stripes under the first sign, one under the second, and two midway between them. The number of stripes does not mean the number of tracks.
1.3.1 and 1.3.2 (a white cross with a red border) stand directly in front of a level crossing without a barrier: 1.3.1 - one track, 1.3.2 - two or more.
1.5 - crossing with a tram line: outside an intersection the tram has priority ⟦14⟧. 1.6 - intersection of roads of equal status, give way to those on your right ⟦15⟧. 1.8 - traffic lights ahead.
1.16.1 - speed hump. 1.19 - a section with two-way traffic begins. 1.21 - a children's institution is nearby, and children may appear on the road.
1.20 - pedestrian crossing ahead; the crossing itself is marked by signs 5.16.1, 5.16.2 and (or) zebra crossing markings.
1.29 - a tunnel without lighting or with a poorly visible entrance. In any tunnel you must not stop or make a U-turn ⟦16⟧.
lesson.tip: A triangle says “danger ahead”, not “stop”: the right reaction is to slow down in advance and be ready for the situation.

p: These signs decide who goes first at an uncontrolled intersection or a narrow section. They have special shapes: a yellow diamond, an inverted triangle and a red octagon with the word STOP.
list: 2.1 “Priority road” (a yellow diamond) - you have priority when passing uncontrolled intersections. 2.2 - end of the priority road. Outside built-up areas, parking on the carriageway of a road with sign 2.1 is prohibited ⟦17⟧.
2.3.1-2.3.7 (a triangle with a thick and a thin line) - you are on the priority road, and ahead a minor road crosses it or joins it.

2.4 “Give way” (an inverted triangle) - give way to vehicles on the road being crossed, or, with plate 7.13, to those on the priority road. Plate 7.1.2 under sign 2.4 shows how many metres ahead the intersection with sign 2.5 is.

2.5 “No passing without stopping (Stop)” - you must stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, before the edge of the carriageway being crossed, and give way. Before a level crossing or a quarantine checkpoint with no stop line, you stop in front of the sign itself.

2.6 (a white circle with a red border and two arrows) - do not enter a narrow section if this would obstruct oncoming traffic; give way to oncoming vehicles. 2.7 (a blue square) - on a narrow section you have priority.
lesson.tip: Sign 2.5 requires you to stop even at an empty intersection. Sign 2.4 only requires you to give way.

lesson.h: Priority road, traffic lights and priority signs
p: The priority road is the one marked by signs 2.1, 2.3.1-2.3.3 or 5.1, and also a paved road in relation to a dirt road, even after sign 2.2 ⟦18⟧. At an intersection of roads of unequal status, a driver on the minor road gives way to everyone on the priority road, whichever way they are going ⟦19⟧.

If the priority road turns at the intersection (this can be seen from plate 7.13), drivers on the priority road pass one another as on roads of equal status. Drivers on minor roads also pass one another in the same way ⟦20⟧.

At an intersection where the order is set by traffic lights or a traffic controller, priority signs do not decide who goes first. But if the traffic light flashes amber or is switched off, the intersection becomes uncontrolled, and the priority signs apply again ⟦21⟧.
lesson.tip: First check whether the traffic light is working. If it is, follow it. If it flashes amber or is off, follow the priority signs.

p: A circle with a red border introduces a prohibition or restriction. Signs 3.27-3.30 with a blue field concern stopping and parking.
list: 3.1 “No entry” - you must not enter in this direction. 3.2 “Closed to all vehicles” - no travel in either direction.
3.3 - motor vehicles are prohibited, that is, those with an engine, including mopeds and electric cars. Ordinary bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles do not count as motor vehicles ⟦22⟧.

3.4 - trucks and road trains with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t (or more than the figure shown on the sign) are prohibited, as well as tractors and self-propelled machines. What matters is the maximum authorised mass, not the load. Trucks with a diagonal white stripe on the sides and trucks for carrying people may proceed.

3.5 - motorcycles and mopeds; 3.6 - tractors and self-propelled machines; 3.7 - trucks and tractors with trailers, and also towing (a passenger car with a trailer may proceed); 3.8 - horse-drawn carts, ridden and pack animals, driving of livestock; 3.9 - bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles; 3.9.1 - e-scooters only; 3.10 - pedestrians.
3.11 limits the actual mass, 3.12 - the actual axle load, 3.13-3.15 - height, width and length including the load (for a road train, the length of the whole road train).

3.16 - keep a following distance of at least the one shown. 3.17.1 and 3.17.3 - stop at customs or a checkpoint; 3.17.2 - further travel is prohibited because of a road traffic accident, an incident or another hazard.

3.20 - overtaking is prohibited, except for vehicles without a trailer that are moving slower than 30 km/h. 3.22 - the same for trucks over 3.5 t, and tractors may overtake only horse-drawn carts and bicycles.
3.24 - do not exceed the speed shown. 3.26 - do not use the horn, except when necessary to prevent a road traffic accident.

3.27 - you may neither stop nor park. 3.28 - parking is prohibited, but you may stop: for up to 5 minutes, or longer for boarding, alighting or loading. 3.29 and 3.30 - parking is prohibited on odd days and even days of the month respectively; if they stand together, vehicles are moved from 19 to 21 h.
lesson.tip: 3.4 looks at the maximum authorised mass, while 3.11 looks at the actual mass: an empty 12 t truck will not pass sign 3.4, but will pass sign 3.11 showing 10 t.

lesson.h: Zone of application of prohibitory signs
p: Signs 3.16, 3.20, 3.22, 3.24 and 3.26-3.30 apply from where they are placed to the nearest intersection beyond them, or, in a built-up area with no intersections, to its end. Exits from adjacent areas (yards, filling stations, parking areas) and junctions of field and forest tracks are not counted as intersections and do not interrupt the zone ⟦23⟧.

The zone can be ended earlier: for 3.16 and 3.26, by plate 7.2.1; for 3.20, 3.22 and 3.24, by signs 3.21, 3.23 and 3.25 or plate 7.2.1, and for 3.24 also by another sign 3.24 showing a different number; for 3.27-3.30, by a repeated sign with plate 7.2.3 or by plate 7.2.2. If sign 3.27 is used with the solid yellow line 1.4, and 3.28 with the broken yellow line 1.10, the zone equals the length of the line. Sign 3.31 cancels all these restrictions at once.
Sign 3.24 placed before a built-up area applies up to sign 5.22.
list: 3.10 and 3.27-3.30 apply only on the side of the road where they are placed.
3.2-3.9, 3.32 and 3.33 prohibit travel in both directions.
3.18.1 and 3.18.2 apply only at the intersection in front of which they are placed.
lesson.tip: You have passed an intersection - the zone “to the nearest intersection” has ended. You have passed the exit from a yard or a field track - it has not.

lesson.h: Who prohibitory signs do not apply to
list: 3.1-3.3, 3.18.1, 3.18.2, 3.19 and 3.27 do not apply to route vehicles (a bus, trolleybus or tram on a route). A taxi is not a route vehicle.

3.2-3.8 do not apply to vehicles that serve organisations or citizens in the zone, or that belong to those who live or work there. They must enter and leave at the intersection nearest to their destination. This exception does not apply to sign 3.1.
3.28-3.30 do not apply to taxis with the taximeter switched on. Taxis must obey sign 3.27.
3.2, 3.3 and 3.28-3.30 do not apply to vehicles driven by persons with Group I and II disabilities, or Group III with musculoskeletal impairments, or carrying such persons.
Plate 7.18 exempts motorised invalid carriages and cars bearing the “Person with a disability” sign from the requirements of the sign ⟦24⟧.
lesson.tip: A resident of the street may drive in past signs 3.2-3.8, but not past the “No entry” sign 3.1: there the exception is only for route vehicles.

p: A blue circle with a white picture says: you may move only as shown. All other directions or kinds of movement are prohibited.
list: 4.1.1-4.1.6 set the permitted directions at the intersection in front of which the sign stands. A sign that permits a left turn also permits a U-turn. Route vehicles may disregard these signs.
4.1.1 at the start of a section of road applies up to the nearest intersection and does not prohibit a right turn into yards and other adjacent areas, but a left turn there is not allowed.
4.2.1-4.2.3 show on which side to drive around an obstacle: right, left or either side. 4.3 - roundabout, in the direction of the arrows.

4.4 - passenger cars, buses, motorcycles, route vehicles and trucks up to 3.5 t are permitted. Others may enter only if they serve this zone or are going to a home or workplace in it, entering at the intersection nearest to their destination.
4.5 - cycle track or lane: bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles only. 4.6 - footpath: pedestrians only, and a moped may only be pushed alongside ⟦25⟧.
4.7 - do not drive slower than the speed shown; the end of the zone is sign 4.8. 4.9.1-4.9.3 show where vehicles bearing the “Dangerous goods” identification signs may go.
lesson.tip: Do not confuse 4.7 (blue circle, minimum speed) with 3.24 (red border, maximum speed).

p: These signs introduce or cancel special traffic regimes and show where things are. Most often they are blue rectangles.
list: 5.1 “Motorway” and 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles” (for motor cars and motorcycles only): you must not make a U-turn or drive into gaps in the central reservation, reverse, do learner driving, stop outside areas marked by 5.15 or 6.11, or drive a vehicle slower than 40 km/h; trucks over 3.5 t may not go beyond the second lane ⟦26⟧. The end is marked by signs 5.2 and 5.4.
5.5 - a one-way road, 5.6 - its end, 5.7.1 and 5.7.2 - entry to such a road: the arrow shows where the traffic flows.

5.8.1 and 5.8.2 - directions by lane; from the far left lane with a left arrow you may also make a U-turn. A sign before an intersection applies to the whole intersection. If sign 5.8.3 shows sign 4.7 and you cannot drive at that speed, move into the additional lane.

5.9 - lane for route vehicles: only public transport (including taxis) and M3 category vehicles, as well as bicycles and e-scooters, may drive and stop on it ⟦27⟧. Other drivers give way to those on this lane when turning ⟦28⟧.
5.11.1 and 5.11.2 - a place and a zone for U-turns; a left turn there is prohibited.

5.16.1 and 5.16.2 - the pedestrian crossing itself. If there are no zebra crossing markings, 5.16.2 is placed on the right at the near edge of the crossing and 5.16.1 on the left at the far edge, and the width of the crossing is the distance between them.
5.18.1 - recommended speed: advice, not a prohibition. It applies up to the nearest intersection, and together with a warning sign, to the end of the hazardous section.

On direction signs outside built-up areas, a green background means the route along a motorway, and blue means a route along another road; in a town, a white background means an object in the same town.

5.22 (white background) - start of a built-up area with its rules: 60 km/h and no use of the horn before overtaking ⟦29⟧. 5.23 - its end. 5.24 (blue background) - only the name: the rules for built-up areas do not apply on this road.
5.35 - reversible traffic: lane-control signals show whether you may use the lane. 5.42 - photo and video enforcement; a camera may operate even where this sign is absent.

p: Some signs mark not a section up to an intersection but a whole area. The regime applies throughout the zone until you see the sign marking its end.
list: 5.38 “Residential zone” (end - 5.39): no faster than 20 km/h; pedestrians walk on the carriageway too and have priority; through traffic, learner driving, parking with the engine running (except electric cars) and use of the horn are prohibited. When leaving, give way to everyone ⟦30⟧.
5.44 and 5.45 - a parking restriction zone; 5.46 and 5.47 - a maximum speed limit zone.
5.48 and 5.49 - a pedestrian zone: only pedestrians may move there.
5.50 and 5.51 - an environmental class restriction zone: you may not enter if the class of your vehicle is lower than the one shown or is not stated in the registration documents.
lesson.tip: A zone sign does not end at an intersection: look for the sign marking the end of the zone.

p: A blue rectangle with a white field and a picture tells you where a useful facility is: a first aid station (6.1), a hospital (6.2), a filling station (6.3), vehicle service (6.4), a car wash (6.5), food (6.7), a rest area (6.11) and others. Plate 7.1.3 or 7.1.4 with an arrow shows that the facility is off the road, and the distance to it.

These signs prohibit nothing and oblige nothing; they only inform. But one of them matters for the test: on a motorway it is prohibited to stop outside the parking areas marked by signs 5.15 or 6.11 ⟦31⟧.

A plate is placed directly under the sign it applies to; only plates 7.2.2-7.2.4 and 7.13 at signs over the road are hung at the side. A plate clarifies a sign: where the hazard begins, how far the prohibition applies, to whom, and on which days and at what times.
list: 7.1.1 - distance to the hazardous section or the place where a restriction begins; 7.1.2 - distance from sign 2.4 to the intersection with sign 2.5; 7.1.3 and 7.1.4 - distance to a facility off the road.
7.2.1 - length of the hazardous section or zone of application of the sign; 7.2.2-7.2.6 - zone of signs 3.27-3.30: length, end, “you are in the zone”, direction along a building frontage or square.
7.3.1-7.3.3 - in which direction from the intersection the sign applies.
7.4.1-7.4.8 - which type of vehicle the sign applies to (7.4.1 - trucks, 7.4.3 - passenger cars and trucks up to 3.5 t); 7.4.9-7.4.14 - which type it does not apply to.
7.5.1-7.5.7 - days and times the sign applies; 7.16 - the sign applies only when the surface is wet; 7.11 - the sign concerns only vehicles with a maximum authorised mass above the figure shown.

With parking place 5.15: 7.6.1 - park on the carriageway alongside the pavement, 7.7 - only with the engine off, 7.9 - maximum parking time, 7.10 - there is a ramp (flyover) or an inspection pit, 7.17 - only for vehicles with the “Person with a disability” sign, 7.22 - only for electric cars and hybrids charged from an external source.
7.13 - direction of the priority road; 7.14 - the lane to which the sign or traffic light applies; 7.15 - the crossing is used by blind pedestrians; 7.21 - a tow truck is operating.
lesson.tip: Under sign 2.4 or 2.5 with plate 7.13, you must give way to those on the priority road (the thick line on the plate).

lesson.h: What overrides what: traffic controller, traffic lights, signs, markings
list: The traffic controller overrides everything: you obey their signals even if they contradict traffic lights, signs or road markings ⟦32⟧.

At a controlled intersection, the order is set by the traffic lights. With a flashing amber or switched-off traffic light, the priority signs apply ⟦33⟧. A green arrow to the left also permits a U-turn, unless a sign prohibits it ⟦34⟧.
If a temporary sign on a portable stand (on a yellow background) contradicts a permanent one, follow the temporary one ⟦35⟧.
If signs, including temporary ones, contradict road markings, or the markings are hard to see, follow the signs ⟦36⟧.
Signs and markings often work as a pair: a crossing is marked by signs 5.16.1, 5.16.2 and (or) markings 1.14.1-1.14.3 ⟦37⟧, and the place to stop at a red light by stop line 1.12 or sign 5.33 ⟦38⟧.
lesson.tip: The traffic controller overrides everything. At an intersection with traffic lights, the order is set by the lights, not by priority signs. Temporary signs override permanent ones, and signs override markings.

keyFacts: Warning signs are placed 150-300 m before the hazardous section outside built-up areas and 50-100 m in built-up areas; a different distance is shown by plate 7.1.1 ⟦1⟧
Outside built-up areas, signs 1.1, 1.2, 1.9, 1.10, 1.21 and 1.23 are repeated, the second one at least 50 m before the hazardous section ⟦2⟧

Sign 2.5 requires you to stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, before the edge of the carriageway being crossed; at a level crossing or quarantine checkpoint with no stop line, before the sign ⟦3⟧
With a flashing amber or switched-off traffic light, the intersection is uncontrolled and priority signs apply ⟦4⟧

Zone of application of 3.16, 3.20, 3.22, 3.24 and 3.26-3.30: up to the nearest intersection, in a built-up area with no intersections up to its end; exits from yards and field tracks do not interrupt it ⟦5⟧
Sign 3.20 does not prohibit overtaking vehicles without a trailer that are moving slower than 30 km/h ⟦6⟧
Signs 3.10 and 3.27-3.30 apply only on their own side of the road, while 3.2-3.9, 3.32 and 3.33 apply in both directions ⟦7⟧

Route vehicles may disregard 3.1-3.3, 3.18.1, 3.18.2, 3.19, 3.27 and 4.1.1-4.1.6; taxis with the taximeter on - 3.28-3.30; persons with Group I, II and III (with musculoskeletal impairments) disabilities - 3.2, 3.3, 3.28-3.30 (Annex 1, Chapters 3, 4)
A sign that permits a left turn also permits a U-turn ⟦8⟧
After sign 5.22 - no faster than 60 km/h, in the residential zone 5.38 - no faster than 20 km/h ⟦9⟧
The traffic controller's signals override traffic lights, signs and road markings ⟦10⟧
Temporary signs on a yellow background override permanent ones, and signs override road markings ⟦11⟧
mistakes: They think sign 2.4 always requires you to stop. Stopping is mandatory at sign 2.5, while 2.4 only requires you to give way.
They think 3.24 applies “until the next sign”. If there is no earlier sign 3.25, 3.31 or plate 7.2.1, the zone ends at the nearest intersection.
They mix up 3.27 and 3.28: under 3.28 you may stop to board or alight, under 3.27 you may not stop even for a minute.
They think residents of the street may drive past the “No entry” sign 3.1. The exception for residents and those serving the zone applies to signs 3.2-3.8, not to 3.1.
They mix up 5.22 and 5.24: built-up area rules (for example, the 60 km/h limit) are introduced by the white sign 5.22, and after the blue 5.24 they do not apply on this road.
They mix up 3.4 and 3.11: sign 3.4 looks at the maximum authorised mass, and 3.11 at the actual mass with the load.

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection with this sign in front of it. What does it require of you?
options: Stop at the edge of the intersection in any case
Give way to vehicles on the road being crossed
Go first: you are on the priority road
Give way only to pedestrians on the crossing
questions.explain: Sign 2.4 requires you to give way to vehicles on the road being crossed, or, with plate 7.13, to those on the priority road. You do not have to stop if you are not impeding anyone.

questions.q: There is this sign in front of the intersection. The road being crossed is empty and visibility is excellent. What should you do?
options: Drive through without stopping, slowing down in advance
Stop only if there are vehicles at the intersection
Always stop, then continue
Sound the horn and drive through without stopping
questions.explain: Sign 2.5 prohibits passing without stopping before the stop line, or, if there is none, before the edge of the carriageway being crossed. You must stop even at an empty intersection, and then give way if anyone appears.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with the “Priority road” sign. A green car is approaching the intersection from a minor road on your right. Who goes first?
options: The green car: it is approaching from the right
You: you are on the priority road
Whoever reached the intersection first
The green car, if it is going straight
questions.explain: You are on the priority road and the green car is on a minor road. At an intersection of roads of unequal status, the driver on the minor road gives way to those on the priority road, regardless of their direction. The “priority to the right” rule applies only on roads of equal status.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with the “Priority road” sign, but the traffic light at the intersection is red for you. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the priority road matters more than the traffic light
Drive on if the road being crossed is empty
Stop only if there is a stop line
Stop: here the traffic light sets the order
questions.explain: An intersection where the order is set by traffic lights is controlled, and priority signs do not decide who goes first there. At a red light you stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, before the carriageway being crossed.

questions.q: The traffic light is flashing amber, and you have the “Give way” sign in front of the intersection. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the blue car
Only the green car
Both
Neither
questions.explain: A flashing amber signal means the intersection is uncontrolled, and priority signs set the order. Under sign 2.4 you give way to everyone on the priority road being crossed, that is, to both the blue and the green car.

questions.q: There is this sign in front of a road narrowing. A truck is approaching the narrow section from the other side, and you will reach the narrowing almost at the same time. What do you do?
options: Enter first, before the truck arrives
Flash your headlights so that the truck stops
Give way and do not enter the narrowing
Go first, keeping close to the shoulder
questions.explain: Sign 2.6 prohibits entering a narrow section if this would obstruct oncoming traffic. You give way to oncoming vehicles that are already on the narrow section or at the opposite entrance to it.

questions.q: There is this sign in front of a narrow section. An oncoming car has reached the narrowing from the other side at the same time as you. Who goes first?
options: The oncoming car: it arrived from the other side
You: you have priority here
Whoever is driving faster
Whoever switches on their headlights first
questions.explain: Sign 2.7 marks a narrow section where you have priority over oncoming vehicles. Oncoming drivers who have sign 2.6 in front of them must give way to you.

questions.q: Under the “Give way” sign in front of you there is a plate, as in the diagram. Who does this sign with the plate require you to give way to?
options: Everyone on the road being crossed
Only vehicles approaching from the right
Those on the priority road (thick line)
Nobody: the plate cancels the whole sign
questions.explain: Plate 7.13 shows the direction of the priority road at the intersection: the thick line. Sign 2.4 with this plate requires you to give way to vehicles on the priority road, and with drivers on minor roads you pass one another by the “priority to the right” rule ⟦39⟧.

questions.q: You live on a street whose entrance from this side is marked by this sign. Can you enter here to reach your home?
options: Yes: this sign does not prohibit residents from entering
Yes, if you enter at the intersection nearest to your home
Yes, if you drive no faster than 20 km/h
No: this sign has no exception for residents
questions.explain: Sign 3.1 prohibits entry by all vehicles in the given direction; the exception is made for route vehicles. The exception for residents and those serving the zone applies to signs 3.2-3.8 and does not apply to sign 3.1.

questions.q: You work in an office located in the zone of this sign. Can you drive there in your own car?
options: No: the exception is only for residents of the zone
Yes, entering at the intersection nearest to the office
Yes, but only until 8 am, while there are no traffic jams
Yes, by any route, if you have a pass
questions.explain: Sign 3.2 does not apply to vehicles that belong to citizens who live or work in the marked zone, or that serve them. You must enter and leave at the intersection nearest to your destination.

questions.q: You are in the zone of this sign, on a road with two lanes in your direction. Ahead in the right lane a tractor without a trailer is travelling at about 25 km/h. May you overtake it in the left lane of your own direction, if there are no other prohibitions?
options: Yes: it has no trailer and is moving slower than 30 km/h
No: the sign prohibits overtaking any vehicle
Yes, but only on the right, on the shoulder
No: tractors may be overtaken only outside the zone
questions.explain: Sign 3.20 prohibits overtaking all vehicles except those without a trailer that are moving slower than 30 km/h. The tractor has no trailer and is moving at about 25 km/h, and to overtake in the left lane of your own direction you do not need to move onto the oncoming side, so overtaking is permitted.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area you have passed this sign and then a filling station exit, as in the diagram. There were no intersections. The truck ahead is doing 60 km/h. May you overtake it?
options: Yes: the filling station exit ended the effect of the sign
No: a filling station exit is not an intersection
Yes: the sign applies for only 100 m
Yes, if the truck signals a right turn
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.20 extends to the nearest intersection. Exits from adjacent areas, such as a filling station, are not counted as intersections and do not interrupt the effect of the sign.

questions.q: In a town this sign is installed, and there are several intersections ahead. There is no sign 3.25 further on. Where will the restriction end?
options: 1 km after the sign
Only at the sign marking the end of the built-up area
At the next traffic light
At the nearest intersection beyond the sign
questions.explain: The zone of sign 3.24 runs from the place of installation to the nearest intersection beyond it. It applies up to the end of the built-up area only if there are no intersections.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area, before the entrance to a village, there is this sign. There are no intersections before the sign marking the start of the built-up area (white background). Up to which point does the restriction apply?
options: Up to the sign marking the start of the built-up area
Up to the end of the built-up area
For 500 m after the sign
Up to the first intersection inside the village
questions.explain: Sign 3.24 installed before a built-up area marked by sign 5.22 applies up to that sign. After it, the rules for built-up areas apply (60 km/h).

questions.q: Can you stop for a minute under this sign to let a passenger out?
options: Yes, if the driver does not get out of the vehicle
Yes, if the hazard warning lights are on
No: the sign prohibits both stopping and parking
Yes, if the stop is shorter than 5 minutes
questions.explain: Sign 3.27 “No stopping” prohibits both stopping and parking, so a passenger may not be let out here even for a minute. The exception from the sign is for route vehicles, not for ordinary drivers.

questions.q: You stopped under this sign to let a passenger out and drove off immediately. Did you break the rules?
options: No: the sign prohibits only parking
Yes, this sign prohibits any stopping of the vehicle
Yes, if the passenger got out onto the carriageway
Yes, if it was during the hours of darkness
questions.explain: Sign 3.28 prohibits parking. A brief stop, including for boarding or alighting of passengers, is permitted under it.

questions.q: Today is the 15th. May you leave your car parked by this sign?
options: Yes, parking is allowed here today
No: parking is prohibited on odd days
Only from 19 to 21 h
You may neither stop nor park
questions.explain: Sign 3.29 prohibits parking on odd days of the month; stopping is permitted. The time 19 to 21 h is when vehicles are moved, if signs 3.29 and 3.30 are used together.

questions.q: This sign stands at the start of a section of road, not before an intersection. Which path may be used to enter the yard?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
questions.explain: Sign 4.1.1 at the start of a section of road applies up to the nearest intersection and does not prohibit a right turn into adjacent areas (A). It does prohibit a left turn into the yard (B).

questions.q: May you make a U-turn at the intersection in front of which this sign stands?
options: No: only ahead or left is permitted
No: a U-turn is permitted only for route vehicles
Only if the intersection has traffic lights
Yes: a left turn also includes a U-turn
questions.explain: Mandatory signs that permit a left turn also permit a U-turn. Sign 4.1.5 permits ahead and left, so a U-turn is also permitted.

questions.q: Who is allowed to use a track with this sign?
options: Bicycles only
Bicycles, mopeds and e-scooters
Bicycles, e-scooters and monowheels
Bicycles and mopeds with an electric motor
questions.explain: Sign 4.5 permits only bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles, for example monowheels. Mopeds may not use it. Pedestrians use a cycle track only if there is no pavement, footpath or shoulder, or if it is impossible to walk on them ⟦40⟧.

questions.q: You have passed this sign with the name of a built-up area; there are no other signs. What is the maximum speed at which you may drive a passenger car?
options: 50 km/h
80 km/h
60 km/h
90 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 5.22 marks the start of a built-up area, where the rules for built-up areas apply: no more than 60 km/h. 50 km/h is the limit for buses and trucks.

questions.q: What does the name of a built-up area on a blue background, as on this sign, mean?
options: The start of a built-up area with a 60 km/h limit
The rules for built-up areas do not apply here
The end of a built-up area
The direction to this built-up area
questions.explain: Sign 5.24 shows the name and start of a built-up area in which, on this road, the requirements of the Rules for built-up areas do not apply. The speed limit stays as outside a built-up area.

questions.q: You have entered the zone marked by this sign. At what speed may you drive?
options: No more than 20 km/h
No more than 40 km/h
No more than 60 km/h
No more than 10 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 5.38 marks a residential zone. In residential zones and residential courtyards, driving is permitted at no more than 20 km/h.

questions.q: You are leaving the zone whose end is marked by this sign onto an ordinary street. Who must you give way to?
options: Nobody, if the street is a minor road
Only vehicles coming from the right
All other road users
Only pedestrians
questions.explain: Sign 5.39 marks the end of the residential zone. When leaving a residential zone, the driver gives way to other road users.

questions.q: What is prohibited on a road marked with this sign?
options: Overtaking in the left lane if it is free
U-turns at central reservation gaps
Passenger cars driving faster than 90 km/h
Driving with dipped headlights in daylight
questions.explain: On a motorway (sign 5.1), U-turns and driving into the gaps in the central reservation are prohibited, as well as reversing and learner driving. Passenger cars may drive there at up to 140 km/h, unless signs require otherwise.

questions.q: You are driving outside a built-up area and see this sign with no plates. Roughly where does the hazardous section begin?
options: Immediately after the sign
After 50-100 m
After 150-300 m
After 500-700 m
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, warning signs are placed 150-300 m before the hazardous section, and in built-up areas 50-100 m. A different distance is shown by plate 7.1.1.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area you passed this sign, and then saw the same one again. What does the second sign mean?
options: A second section starts near another school
The zone of the children's institution has ended
You may increase your speed again
A repeat: at least 50 m to the section with children
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, signs 1.1, 1.2, 1.9, 1.10, 1.21 and 1.23 are repeated. The second sign is placed at least 50 m before the start of the hazardous section, so children may appear very soon.

questions.q: Next to a permanent 60 km/h limit sign, on a portable stand, there is a temporary 40 km/h limit sign on a yellow background. What should you do?
options: No faster than 60 km/h: the permanent sign takes precedence
Choose either of the two signs
No faster than 50 km/h, as the average
No faster than 40 km/h: the temporary sign takes precedence
questions.explain: At road works and where traffic is temporarily changed, temporary signs on a yellow background are used. If a temporary sign contradicts a permanent one, the driver follows the temporary one.

questions.q: You have sign 2.5 in front of the intersection, but the traffic controller is standing sideways to you with arms stretched out to the sides. You are turning right. What should you do?
options: Turn right on the traffic controller's signal
Stop at the stop line anyway: the sign takes precedence
Wait until the traffic controller leaves
Turn only if the traffic light is flashing amber
questions.explain: Drivers obey the traffic controller's signals even if they contradict signs. You see the traffic controller's side with arms stretched out: this permits going straight and turning right. While the traffic controller is directing traffic, the priority signs do not apply.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area there are signs on the right, as in the diagram. Roughly how far is it to the level crossing?
options: At least 50 m: this is the second, repeat sign
The level crossing starts right after these signs
150-300 m: this is the first sign before the crossing
50-100 m, as for signs in a built-up area
questions.explain: Sign 1.4.1 with three stripes is placed under the first sign 1.1 or 1.2 along your route, and the first warning sign outside a built-up area stands 150-300 m before the crossing. Under the second sign (at least 50 m before the crossing), sign 1.4.3 with one stripe is placed.
questions.ref: Annex 1, signs 1.1, 1.4.1-1.4.3 and the general provisions of Chapter 1

questions.q: Outside a built-up area there are signs on the right, as in the diagram. What do they mean?
options: One track passes through the crossing: there is one stripe on the sign
A level crossing without a barrier is close: this is the second sign
There are still 150-300 m to a level crossing with a barrier
The level crossing without a barrier starts right after these signs
questions.explain: Sign 1.2 warns of a level crossing without a barrier, and sign 1.4.3 with one stripe is placed under the second sign 1.1 or 1.2. Outside a built-up area the second sign stands at least 50 m before the crossing. The number of stripes shows how close the crossing is, not the number of tracks.
questions.ref: Annex 1, signs 1.2, 1.4.1-1.4.3 and the general provisions of Chapter 1

questions.q: This sign stands beside the road. Where is the level crossing and what kind is it?
options: In 150-300 m, a crossing with a barrier
Right here, without a barrier, one track
In 50-100 m, a crossing with a barrier and traffic lights
Right here, without a barrier, two or more tracks
questions.explain: Signs 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 mark a level crossing without a barrier and stand directly in front of it. Sign 1.3.2 is used if there are two or more tracks, and 1.3.1 if there is one track.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. There are no priority signs or traffic lights at the intersection, and both roads are paved. A car is approaching from the right. What should you do?
options: Give way to it: it is approaching from the right
Go first: this sign gives you priority
Go first if you are going straight
Give way only if it is driving faster than you
questions.explain: Sign 1.6 warns of an intersection of roads of equal status. At such an intersection the driver gives way to vehicles approaching from the right.

questions.q: You are driving in a town and see this sign. What does it tell you?
options: In 150-300 m there are traffic lights, which are currently off
The traffic lights ahead are broken, and priority signs apply
Right after the sign, traffic is controlled by a traffic controller
In 50-100 m there is a section where traffic lights operate
questions.explain: Sign 1.8 warns of an intersection, pedestrian crossing or section of road controlled by traffic lights. In a built-up area, warning signs are placed 50-100 m before such a place.
questions.ref: Annex 1, sign 1.8 and the general provisions of Chapter 1

questions.q: This sign stands right at the start of a descent, with no distance plate. The descent comes straight after an ascent. Is the sign installed correctly?
options: No: outside a built-up area it is placed 150-300 m before
No: without plate 7.1.1 it is invalid
Yes, but this is allowed only in a built-up area
Yes: if descents and ascents follow one another, this is allowed
questions.explain: Warning signs are usually placed in advance. But signs 1.13 and 1.14 may be installed without plate 7.1.1 directly at the start of a descent or ascent, if descents and ascents follow one another.

questions.q: On a town street this sign stands only 10-15 m before a repair crew, with no plate under it. How should this be understood?
options: The works are short-term: placing the sign this way is permitted
The sign is wrongly placed, so it can be ignored
The works will start only 50-100 m from the sign
The works are finished, and the sign was simply forgotten
questions.explain: Sign 1.23 may be placed without plate 7.1.1 only 10-15 m before the works when the works on the carriageway are short-term. Slow down and be ready to drive around the workers.

questions.q: You see a sign with a plate, as in the diagram. Where will the slippery section begin?
options: Right after the sign, and the section is 150 m long
In 150-300 m, and the plate does not matter here
It began 150 m ago
About 150 m from the sign
questions.explain: Plate 7.1.1 shows the distance from the sign to the start of the hazardous section. The length of the section would be shown by a different plate, 7.2.1 with up and down arrows.

questions.q: You see a sign with a plate, as in the diagram. What does the plate mean?
options: The slippery section starts in 500 m
The slippery section extends for 500 m
You may not drive faster than 50 km/h on the section
In 500 m the sign will stop applying if there is no intersection
questions.explain: Plate 7.2.1 with arrows shows the length of the hazardous section (for prohibitory signs, their zone of application). The distance to the start of the section would be shown by plate 7.1.1 without arrows.

questions.q: In a town you see this sign with no plate. What is the best thing to do?
options: Slow down in advance: the hump is in 50-100 m
Stop before the hump and drive over it from a standstill
Drive around the hump in the oncoming lane
Change nothing: the sign concerns only trucks
questions.explain: Sign 1.16.1 warns of a speed hump. In a built-up area it is placed 50-100 m before the hump, so you should slow down in advance to drive over it smoothly.
questions.ref: Annex 1, sign 1.16.1 and the general provisions of Chapter 1; para. 72

questions.q: You are driving in the left lane of a one-way road and see this sign. What should you do?
options: Carry on in the left lane: the sign only warns
Stop and let the oncoming vehicles through
Move right: oncoming traffic will start soon
Switch on the hazard warning lights and carry on
questions.explain: Sign 1.19 warns that a section of road with two-way traffic begins ahead. There, the left half of the carriageway is for oncoming vehicles, so move over to the right in advance.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. What is prohibited in the tunnel ahead?
options: Stopping and making a U-turn
Driving with dipped headlights on
Driving faster than 40 km/h
Changing lanes if there are several
questions.explain: Sign 1.29 warns of a tunnel without artificial lighting or with a poorly visible entrance. Stopping and making a U-turn are prohibited in any tunnel, and therefore reversing too.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. Just after the bend you can see the road for less than 100 m. May you stop on the carriageway beyond the bend?
options: Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if the stop is no longer than 5 minutes
No: stopping is prohibited here
Yes, but only to let a passenger out
questions.explain: Stopping on the carriageway near dangerous bends is prohibited if visibility of the road is less than 100 m in at least one direction. A driver behind you may not have time to notice you.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. Bends restrict your view, and you can see the road for less than 100 m. May you overtake a slow car by moving into the oncoming lane?
options: Yes: a warning sign does not prohibit overtaking
Yes, if you sound the horn in advance
No: such overtaking is prohibited when the view is restricted
Yes, if it is moving slower than 30 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 1.12.1 itself does not prohibit overtaking; it warns of dangerous bends. But visibility here is less than 100 m, that is, restricted, and on such sections overtaking by moving into the oncoming lane is prohibited.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area you have passed this sign. A cycle track crosses the road outside an intersection, with no traffic lights or priority signs there. A cyclist is approaching the crossing from the right. Who must give way?
options: You: the cyclist is approaching from the right
The cyclist: they give way to vehicles on the road
You: the cyclist has priority on a cycle track
Whoever reaches the crossing a moment later
questions.explain: Sign 1.22 warns of a crossing with a cycle track. At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track and a road outside an intersection, the cyclist gives way to vehicles travelling on the road. But be ready to brake if the cyclist does not notice you.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with a sign as in the diagram. From the joining road on your right, a green car is pulling out to the left. Who goes first?
options: The green car: it is approaching from the right
Whoever reached the intersection first
The green car: it has already started to turn
You: you are on the priority road
questions.explain: Sign 2.3.2 means you are on the priority road and a minor road joins from the right. The green car is pulling out of the minor road and gives way to everyone on the priority road, so you go first.

questions.q: You are pulling out to the left from a joining road, as in the diagram. A blue car is approaching along the priority road from the bottom of the diagram. Who goes first?
options: The blue car: it is on the priority road
You: the blue car is approaching you from the left
You: you have already started to turn
Whoever switched on their direction indicator first
questions.explain: Sign 2.3.2 stands for those on the priority road and shows that a minor road, the one you are on, joins from the right. When pulling out of a minor road you give way to everyone on the priority road, so the blue car goes first.

questions.q: You have passed a sign with a plate, as in the diagram. What will you need to do in 250 m?
options: Stop before the intersection and give way
Give way without stopping if you are not impeding anyone
Drive through the intersection first: you are on the priority road
Stop at the checkpoint for a check
questions.explain: Plate 7.1.2 under sign 2.4 shows the distance to the intersection with sign 2.5 in front of it. There you must stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, before the edge of the carriageway being crossed, and give way.

questions.q: Sign 2.5 “No passing without stopping (Stop)” stands in front of a quarantine checkpoint, with no stop line. Where must you stop?
options: In front of sign 2.5
At the barrier or the checkpoint booth
Where the checkpoint worker indicates: the sign does not matter here
Nowhere, if nobody is at the checkpoint
questions.explain: Sign 2.5 may stand in front of a level crossing or a quarantine checkpoint. In that case the driver stops in front of the stop line, or, if there is none, in front of the sign itself.

questions.q: Outside a built-up area, on a road marked with this sign, a red car is standing on the carriageway and a blue one on the shoulder. Both drivers want to leave their cars for 20 minutes. Who is allowed to?
options: Only the red one
Both
Only the blue one
Neither
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, parking on the carriageway of roads marked with sign 2.1 is prohibited. The red car may only stop for a short time, while the blue car is on the shoulder, where parking is permitted.

questions.q: You have passed a sign, as in the diagram, and are approaching an intersection with a dirt road. There are no other signs. A green car is approaching from the right along the dirt road. Who goes first?
options: The green car: the sign has cancelled your priority road
You: a paved road takes precedence over a dirt road
The green car: it is approaching from the right
Whoever reached the intersection first
questions.explain: Sign 2.2 means the end of the priority road marked by signs. But a paved road is still the priority road in relation to a dirt road, so the green car gives way to you.

questions.q: You are driving on the priority road, as the plate shows, and continuing straight on. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the blue car
Only the green car
Both
Neither
questions.explain: The priority road here turns to the left, and the blue car is also on it. Drivers on the priority road pass one another as at an intersection of roads of equal status: the blue car is approaching from the left, so it gives way. The green car is on the minor road and is driving straight towards you, so your paths do not cross.

questions.q: You are on a minor road, as the plate shows, and driving straight on. Who must you give way to?
options: Only the blue car
Only the green car
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Plate 7.13 shows that the priority road turns: in the diagram it goes from the bottom to the left, and the blue and green cars are both on it. Only the blue car's path crosses yours, and you give way to it. The green car is coming towards you straight ahead, your paths do not cross, and you cause it no obstruction.
